Is there enough evidence

Plan the sample before looking for a winner. Challenge a promising result against assignment quality, uncertainty and user-experience harm.

Planning and synthetic examples

No real experiment is running. This page collects no events, stores no identifiers and never reads your live analytics.

GoatCounter visits are aggregate estimates. They do not establish independent randomized participants or unique-user conversion rates.

Define a meaningful change

Equal 50/50 allocation, two-sided 5% significance, 80% power; normal approximation. Daily traffic is a planning assumption. The outcome window must mature after enrollment.

A result must pass more than one check

Intervals use Wilson/Newcombe differences. Allocation mismatch uses a chi-square check at 0.1%. The error guardrail requires its upper interval below a predeclared 0.50 percentage-point harm margin.

Examples assume independent randomized users, one binary outcome per user, a fixed horizon and mature outcomes. Aggregate counts cannot prove those assumptions. Do not repeatedly peek, change the metric after seeing results, or interpret a failed quality check as product lift.

Before a real test

Write the hypothesis, randomization unit, primary metric, guardrails, exclusion rules, exposure contract, sample size, horizon and stopping policy. Verify assignment and event delivery, then obtain the required privacy and product approvals. Low traffic can make a usability study more informative than an underpowered A/B test.

Review the reproducible statistical checks and instrumentation boundary.
